input: My LED connected to Pin 13 is not blinking even though the sketch uploaded successfully. Here is the sketch: void setup() { pinMode(13, OUTPUT); } void loop() { digitalWrite(13, HIGH); }
expected_output: The LED needs to be toggled with a delay (LOW then HIGH) to blink. Also check if the cathode is connected to GND with an appropriate current-limiting resistor.
context: Arduino Uno digital output pins provide 5V. LEDs require a current-limiting resistor (e.g. 220 ohm) in series to ground. Blinking requires state toggling with delay().

metadata.circuitFlaw: Missing delay and state toggle in loop; verify GND path

input: I have a push button connected to Pin 2, but digitalRead(2) keeps returning random HIGH and LOW values when not pressed.
expected_output: The pin is floating because there is no pull-up or pull-down resistor. Use pinMode(2, INPUT_PULLUP) to enable the internal pull-up resistor.
context: Digital input pins on ATmega328P are high-impedance. A floating pin picks up electromagnetic noise unless tied to VCC or GND via a pull-up/down resistor or internal pull-up.

metadata.circuitFlaw: Floating input pin without pull-up/down reference

input: My I2C OLED display (SSD1306) is not showing anything on Arduino Uno. Connected SDA to Pin 4 and SCL to Pin 5.
expected_output: On an Arduino Uno, hardware I2C pins are A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL), not digital pins 4 and 5. Reconnect SDA to A4 and SCL to A5.
context: Arduino Uno (ATmega328P) dedicated TWI/I2C pins are mapped to Analog pins A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL). Digital pins 4 and 5 cannot be used for standard Wire library hardware I2C.

metadata.circuitFlaw: Incorrect I2C bus wiring on Uno (Digital 4/5 instead of A4/A5)
